properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 29 at 11:16AM MST until October 30 at 10:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Yavapai County and northern Gila County. This includes Oak
Creek and Sycamore Canyons.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A second round of rain and thunderstorms is expected Saturday
night through the early morning hours of Monday. An additional 1
to 3 inches of rain will be possible, on top of already saturated
ground, increasing the threat of flooding.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

Consider changing your plans if you were going to hike, boat, or
paddleboard to a slot canyon or normally dry wash. If you do still
decide to recreate, check in at a nearby visitor center or ranger
station.

properties.description:

possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central New Mexico, including the following
area, South Central Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

will be lower.

properties.description:
A trough over the eastern half of the state will continue to focus
return showers to the islands through the day. Pockets of heavy rain
and isolated thunderstorms may produce flash flooding over Maui and
Hawaii Counties.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Molokai, Lanai, Maui, Kahoolawe and Big Island.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed
due to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may
receive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid
runoff.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A trough continues to lay over the eastern half of the state
within a very moist and fairly unstable environment. Energy
moving up from the southwest may initiate return periods of
moderate to locally heavy rainfall. This rain has a high
probability of focusing on Maui and Hawaii Counties. Locally
moderate to heavy showers, with possible isolated thunderstorms,
may produce short-lived intense rain rates through the day.
